title: Rust: ragtime bands versus jazz, and thanks
summary: Rust argues Sousa, Pryor and others played written ragtime, while the ODJB were the first jazz recordings; he closes his statement.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: it's easy enough to listen to them. I've only got to listen to those and compare them with the original Dixieland Jazz Band to realise that the one is Ragtime and the other is Jazz. The original Dixieland Jazz Band isn't called Jazz for Nothing. There are other musicians having laid claim to having made the first jazz records. I have just compiled a book which lays great stress on the dates of recordings. The first jazz recordings in the book, not Ragtime, the first jazz recordings, are those by the original Dixieland Jazz Band. Wilbur Swetman came some time afterwards, so did Earl Fuller, so did Ted Lewis. The bands that came before that are Ragtime bands. There was Sousa's band, there was Arthur Pryor's band, they all played Ragtime. If you doubt that, read Rudy Blesch's book of that name, they all played Ragtime. He gives a great deal of space to describing Sousa's band when they played Ragtime. And to the banjoists like Vess Osman, they played Ragtime. They didn't play jazz though. They played Ragtime. It was all written down and they played everything as written. They couldn't do otherwise. They weren't fakers. They couldn't play. They hadn't got any invention at all in them. They played what was written and that was that. It may have been good or it may have been bad. We're not concerned with that at this date. This was Ragtime. It was played off the score. Jazz was played as the musicians felt under the directorship of my good friend here, Mr. La Rocca. Well, I don't think there's anything much else I can say except that this has been a really great privilege to me and there's only one thing that I wish, that is I could stay longer here in this wonderful city. The only thing I hate about New Orleans is leaving it.
